candidates.title: Ehrenberg-Bass: modernising packaging only works if distinctive brand cues survive (Tropicana 2009, Bahlsen 2021)
candidates.claim: Dr William Caruso, Journal of Retailing and Consumer Services (2026, doi 10.1016/j.jretconser.2026.104800), survey of primary household shoppers in US and UK (sample size not stated in release): redesign succeeds when it raises perceived modernity without removing recognisable cues; removing colours, logos or layout can cut familiarity and purchase intent; 58% of marketers say modernisation was the main purpose of their latest pack redesign; modernise when pack likeability has measurably declined; use Distinctive Asset Testing.
candidates.note: SELECTED. Evergreen idea with a fresh academic spark; release is April 2026, so do not call it 'new' on screen.

lenses.verification: Primary university release read; case figures cross-checked: Tropicana unit sales -20% Jan 1-Feb 22 2009, about $33M (IRI via Bloomberg Businessweek, 2009-04-02); reverted after under two months. Bahlsen -11.8% Jan-May 2023 per CEO in Lebensmittelzeitung (via Creative Bloq), redesign won D&AD; commentators note inflation also played a part -> say 'sales fell' not 'the design caused all of it'. Sample size of the survey unknown: no study numbers on screen except the 58% if attributed in caption.
lenses.audience_psychology: Every owner has felt the urge to 'refresh the logo'; seeing an award-winning redesign lose shoppers creates loss-aversion tension and a self-check ('what do my customers actually recognise?'). Strong save/share.
lenses.brand_fit: Core to a brand designer-strategist: argues for strategy over decoration, positions the studio as the one that protects equity. Works identically for Persian and international English viewers.

lenses_summary.verification_red_team: C01's academic finding comes from a university release (sample size not given); the two cases are well documented: Tropicana -20% unit sales in under two months (IRI via Businessweek 2009), Bahlsen -11.8% Jan-May 2023 (CEO via Lebensmittelzeitung), but Bahlsen's fall was also during high inflation, so the reel must not claim the design alone caused it. No invented numbers; at most one number on screen (Tropicana 20%).
lenses_summary.audience_psychology: Loss aversion plus recognition: 'your customers don't read your pack, they recognise it'. Every viewer has hunted for a familiar product on a shelf and walked past it after a redesign. Gives owners an instant self-test.
lenses_summary.brand_fit: Lets a designer argue against cosmetic redesign, building trust with serious clients. Distinct from yesterday's Jif (usage moments) though both touch packaging; this one is about identity/distinctive assets.

fail_or_weak: C05/C08 repeated from yesterday's pool, weak tension

story.winner: C01 (with C02 and C03 as its cases)
story.why: Sharpest tension (the redesign that won a design award and lost shoppers) and the most concrete image (an orange with a straw replaced by a glass of juice, and shoppers walking past it).
